text: The depth axis, declared as the semantic tokens tokens.css read in each place before the axis existed: the fills are the accent, the faces the surface, the tints the soft accent, the linked rows the second surface, the borders, the off track and the focused edge the strong line, the rim the line, the danger fill the negative tone; the highlights, shadows, sheen and press are transparent and 0. tokens.css reads every one of these, so a theme cannot leave them out; it can only turn them off or point them back, which is what this does, so this theme renders as it did, and an app's override of --rst-accent, --rst-surface or --rst-line on :root still reaches the controls it reached before (Astra A2).
context: One comment above the new tokens in plain.css and signal.css, files an app owns as static/theme.css. A developer reads it when wondering why a flat theme declares depth.
notes: English only; a comment in a file the app owns. Astra A2: the tokens were copies of the stock colours, so an app's semantic overrides stopped reaching them; they are aliases now and the comment says so.

text: Accent. One colour an app sets; the rest follow it. The link hover, the tints, the halo, the plain sheen and the rim fold the accent into black, white, a surface or transparent with color-mix(in srgb), every share a literal percentage: calc(var()) in a color-mix() percentage invalidates the whole declaration in Safari (A4). The four fills and the soft ground take the accent's hue at day's own lightness, because in dark the accent is a light text blue and no mix of it with black or a surface reaches a deep button fill. Those five are declared here as day's cobalt and derived in the @supports block after this one, which an engine without relative colour skips. The fallback inside each var() applies only when --rst-accent is unset or set to initial: a custom property accepts any tokens, so a malformed override is valid as far as var() can tell and blanks every derived colour. With the default accent each derived value lands within two units per channel of the hex it replaced, and the contrast table above is computed from the resolved values.
context: A comment above the accent tokens in day.css. A developer reads it before overriding the accent or adding a derived token.
notes: draft; English only; not in Appendix C. Added with Task 11b, which derives the fills, tints, focus and light colours from --rst-accent.

text: The five hue-derived tokens, redeclared where the engine has relative colour syntax. oklch(from) needs Chrome 119, Safari 16.4 and Firefox 128, and Firefox 128 is above the floor (Chrome 123, Safari 17.5, Firefox 121). Without this gate an older engine would resolve the fill to nothing at the use site and paint a white label on a white button; below it the :root values hold, day's cobalt, which an accent override does not reach. The lightness is day's own. The chroma is the accent's, scaled to day's and capped, so a grey accent gives a grey fill rather than a vivid one at a powerless hue. The fill and the hover fill lower their lightness around hue 170, yellow through green to cyan: a colour of that lightness clipped to sRGB gains luminance, and the label sits not on the fill but on the fill under the face shade's 4% white and, hovered, under the sheen's white too, so cyan's dark hover, 4.74:1 on the bare fill, was 4.15:1 on the painted face (Astra A1). The drop is a cosine bump that is zero beyond 85 degrees from 170, so the default cobalt, at hue 263, is outside it and lands where it did; its depth is 0.05 and 0.045 in light and 0.1 and 0.05 in dark, measured against the brightest pixel of the photographed button for twelve hues, three greys and the sRGB edges in TestAnyAccentKeepsTheFillLabelReadable. Every number is a literal, and the only arithmetic is inside a channel, where every engine with relative colour takes calc(), min(), max() and cos().

text:
A press is a number so a release can fade it: a gradient cannot transition, a registered number inside one can.

Every variant composes its own rest, hover, press, focus, disabled and busy from named tokens, in this order, at one specificity, so the cascade never decides a state. The press rules come last. Every token is read through a fallback that is today's value, so a theme written before the axis renders as it did. A filled button's hover reads its own hover fill: a filter on the fill scaled the label too, and an earlier hover rule once won the label back to the accent on the red fill at 1.05:1, at the moment a reader committed to a delete. The face is four background layers: the sheen, the press spot, the press wash, the face shade. The press is instant and the release fades over 0.7s through --rst-press; the strengths are per-scheme number tokens composed as rgb(0 0 0 / calc(press * strength)), because a color-mix() whose percentage carried calc(var()) blanked every button in Safari. The sheen is on while hovered and not pressed, and only where a pointer can hover.

text: A scheme change lands in the frame it happens in. At rest nothing fades its background (the rail items', rows' and tiles' fades sit on their hover rules, so an app's own switch lands with no help); a hovered item's fade is running, and a change of scheme retargets it while the text changes at once: a tenth of a second of new text on the old scheme's ground after the click. getAnimations() flushes style, which starts the transitions, and cancelling one lands it on its end value. Transitions only, told by transitionProperty: cancelling an animation would stop a spinner for good.

text:
light.js: the light. First-party, dependency-free, and deletable: remove this file and its script tag and the page is the still depth design, because every property here has a default the stylesheet already carries.

What it does: lights the page from where the sun is at this hour (from the left in the morning, overhead at noon, from the right in the evening); puts the pointer's position on the button under it, so the button catches a sheen there; puts a press's position on the button, for a mouse and for a touch, so the press darkens most where it landed; and lets a card breathe: its rim brightens near the pointer over about a second and fades when the pointer leaves. The whole page's light can follow the pointer instead: set FOLLOW below to true. It is off because every write of it restyles the page.

What it writes: --rst-light-x and --rst-light-y on the root, from -1 to 1; --rst-mx, --rst-my, --rst-px and --rst-py on a button, in the button's own pixels; --rst-card-x, --rst-card-y and --rst-card-lit on a card. Nothing else. It never writes on a switch, so a drag rastrillo.js owns (data-rst-drag) never meets it.

What it never does: capture the pointer, read a sensor (no ambient light, no tilt: both need a permission or a flag), or run under prefers-reduced-motion or forced colours, where it adds no listener and clears what it wrote if the setting turns on mid-session. One animation frame loop, running only while something is still easing; the hour is read again every five minutes; the loop pauses while the page is hidden.

For a test: dispatch a CustomEvent "rst:light" on the document with detail {x, y, hold}; hold keeps the light there against pointer moves.

text:
**Creative North Star: "A Default With a Point of View"**

This is the interface an application has before anyone has styled it, and it should look like someone chose it. `day` is near-greyscale with hairline borders, one cobalt for anything that acts, crisp corners, and natural depth: light comes from above, cards rest on the page, controls press in and slowly lift. It aims to read as professional, in the family of the tools people already trust, and to be recognisably this system's.

Remixability is still the thesis. Every colour, radius, shadow, highlight and strength resolves through a custom property, and the three shipped themes prove the axes work rather than offering a menu of three answers: `day` turns depth on, `plain` and `signal` turn it off and render as they always did. An app that wants a fourth writes one `:root` block. Files are delivered once and app-owned from that moment: edit them, or delete what you do not use.

text:
- **Interface Blue** (`#1f56d6` light, `#7aa2ff` dark): the accent, a cobalt. It marks what you can act on and where you are: focus rings, links, an active tab, the current menu item. It belongs to the chrome, not to the content. - **Accent Fill** (`#2257df` light, `#2f61e8` dark): the primary button's fill, with a hover fill of its own (`#1d4dc8` light, `#2956d0` dark) and a white label (`on-accent-fill`). A filled control never darkens by filter: every state is a colour, gated. - **Danger Fill** (`#c62f2f` light, `#c43232` dark): the danger button's fill, the same way, with a white label. - **Interface Blue Deep** (`#1844ac` light, `#a3c0ff` dark): kept for a theme written before the fills; `tokens.css` reads it only as the primary hover's fallback. - **Interface Blue Wash** (`#ecf1ff` light, `#16234a` dark): the tint behind a current menu item, and the fallback for the hover and press tints in a theme that declares none. Carries no text of its own beyond the accent and the muted greys, both gated against it.

### Neutral

- **Page** (`#fbfbfc` light, `#0c0d0f` dark): the page ground, one step below the surface, so a card reads as resting on it. - **Surface** (`#ffffff` light, `#141518` dark): cards, panels, inputs and menus. - **Surface Sunken** (`#f3f3f5` light, `#18191d` dark): the recessed step, for table header rows, the second tone in a stack and a hovered ghost button. - **Hairline** (`#e6e6ea` light, `#26282e` dark): every divider, card edge and table rule. - **Control Edge** (`#868691` light, `#71737c` dark): the border of a field and a select. Deliberately much darker than the hairline, and held at 3:1 against its backgrounds because it is a control boundary (WCAG 1.4.11), not decoration. - **Control Border** (`#d0d4dc` light, `#343843` dark): a plain button's edge, softer than the field border on purpose. The label identifies the button, so the edge is decoration under 1.4.11 and carries no 3:1 floor. - **Ink** (`#18181b` light, `#ededf0` dark): body text. - **Ink Muted** (`#52525c` light, `#a1a1aa` dark): secondary text, subheads, cell values that are not the row's name. - **Ink Faint** (`#6b6b75` light, `#8c8c96` dark): hints, captions, counts. Still gated at 4.5:1; "faint" is a role, not a licence to drop below the floor.

text:
## The light

`light.js` moves the light. The shadows' light comes from the hour: the left in the morning, overhead at noon, the right in the evening, so shadows lean away from it by up to 1.5px and the top highlight leans toward it. With a mouse, a button catches a sheen where the pointer is (white on a filled button, a faint accent tint on a plain one in light mode), and a card's rim brightens near the pointer over about a second and fades when it leaves. On a phone a pressed button shows the press, not the sheen, and a tapped card catches the light briefly. The whole page's light can follow the pointer instead: set `FOLLOW` to `true` at the top of the file. It is off because every write of it restyles the page.

It does not run under reduced motion, does nothing under forced colours, reads no sensor, and never captures the pointer. For the still design, delete the file and its script tag, and name it in `vendoredIsMine` in the app's pin test; `rastrillo doctor` then lists it as yours, a recorded edit, and `--fix` leaves it alone.

text:
### Hover and press

Hover is quiet and press is clear. A plain button's hover is a light grey face and a darker border; a filled button's is a deeper fill; a ghost's is a surface tint. Rows, menu items and sidebar items lift: a 5% accent tint (9% in dark), a highlight along the top edge, no sheen. The current sidebar item is a selected thumb, and hovering another is a half-raised preview of it. These tints and lifts apply only on a device that can hover, so a tap leaves no tint behind; the phone index rows keep their tap tint on purpose.

A press is instant and slow to leave. The button drops 1px, loses its highlight and outer shadow for an inset one, switches its sheen off and darkens, most under the pointer; on release the darkness lifts over about 0.7s, the spot under the finger last. A row pressed, or its link tapped, takes a stronger tint and sinks. Under reduced motion nothing moves and nothing fades.

text:
**`day` looks different; your app's copy does not change until you re-copy it.** The default theme now has a point of view: near-greyscale neutrals with hairline borders, cobalt for anything that acts, 6px and 4px corners, and natural depth lit from above. Buttons are a touch proud of the page and press in, then slowly lift; cards rest on the page; the switch's knob is lit in both schemes; rows and menu items lift quietly on hover. A new vendored script, `light.js`, lights the page from the hour, puts a sheen under the pointer, and can be deleted for the still design. `plain` and `signal` render as they did. An existing app keeps its copies until `rastrillo doctor --fix` re-copies `tokens.css`, `theme.css` and `rastrillo.js` and writes `light.js`; a theme of your own keeps rendering as it did, because every new token is read through a fallback that is today's value.

- New vendored file `light.js`, optional. `rastrillo doctor --fix` writes it; link it after `busy.js` in your layout, as the shipped shells do. To turn it off, delete the file, delete its tag, and name it in `vendoredIsMine` in the scaffold's `vendored_test.go`; `doctor` then lists it as yours, a recorded edit, and `--fix` leaves it alone. See [Templates](/docs/templates#the-light). - New theme tokens, declared by every theme: the fills and their edges, the control face and borders, the depth tokens (`--rst-depth-hl`, `-contact`, `-ambient`, `-face`, `--rst-press-drop`), the switch's knob and track, the tints and the focus pair, the light's colours, the press strengths, and the title, heading, label and rail choices. See [Your app's design system](/docs/design-system). - `tokens.css` registers `--rst-press` and reads every new token with a fallback to the old behaviour. - `rastrillo.js` registers a passive `touchstart` listener so iOS applies `:active` on tap. - Hover tints and lifts on buttons, dropdown summaries, menu rows, options, locale and scheme buttons, linked rows, media tiles and the desktop rail items now sit behind `(hover: hover)`, in every theme, so a tap no longer leaves a tint behind on a touch screen. The phone index rows keep their tap tint on purpose. - Sidebar and console rail items fade their hover over 0.2s, and linked rows and media tiles over 0.25s, in every theme. - In `day`, overriding `--rst-accent` alone recolours everything: the primary button's fill, its hover and edges, the link hover, the soft ground, the hover and press tints, the focus edge and halo, a plain button's sheen and a card's lit rim are all derived from it in `day.css`. The fills take the accent's hue at day's own lightness, with the accent's chroma scaled and capped (`oklch(from var(--rst-accent) L C h)`): a grey accent gives a grey button, and the white label clears 4.5:1 for every hue, measured at twelve hues and three greys in both schemes. The rest are `color-mix()` shares of the accent. With the default accent each derived value lands within two units per channel of the hex it replaced, and the contrast rows that name them are recomputed. Relative colour needs Firefox 128, above the floor, so the fills and the soft ground are declared as day's cobalt and derived inside `@supports (color: oklch(from red l c h))`: an older engine keeps the cobalt button and loses only its following of the accent. `plain` and `signal` work as before: their fills (`--rst-accent-fill` and its `-hover`, `-edge` and `-edge-hover`) read `--rst-accent` and `--rst-accent-strong`, and every other new token reads the semantic token `tokens.css` read in its place before (`--rst-accent-soft` for the tints and the current nav item, `--rst-surface-2` for linked rows, `--rst-line-strong` for control borders, `--rst-tone-negative-fg` for the danger button, and so on), so an app that overrides those on `:root` still reaches what it reached before. - A card's hairline is painted as a background layer. An app stylesheet that sets `background` on a card loses the hairline, and one that sets `background-color` paints under the face and shows nothing; set `--rst-surface` on the card instead, which also recolours the surfaces inside it. - Dropdowns in a shell's tail, meaning the locale and scheme menus and any app dropdown placed there, wear no button face in `day`. - The colour-scheme switch lands in one frame: `rastrillo.js` cancels running CSS transitions on a flip, so text and ground change together. - Forced colours and print get their own blocks, in every theme: real borders, no shadows, filled buttons as outlined text.

## The light

`static/light.js` moves the light the depth styles read: the shadows' light comes from the hour, a button catches a sheen under the pointer, and a card's rim brightens near it. text: Every component paints itself from these. In `day` that one line changes the accent everywhere: the fills take its hue at the theme's own lightness, with its chroma scaled and capped, so a grey accent gives a grey button and a white label reads on any hue; the tints, the focus ring and the light's colours are mixed from it. ### Shadow Vocabulary (the `day` theme)

- **Pop** (`0 2px 4px light-dark(rgba(16,24,40,0.06), rgba(0,0,0,0.35)), 0 8px 16px -4px light-dark(rgba(16,24,40,0.1), rgba(0,0,0,0.5))`): an open menu, a dropdown panel, a modal: surfaces that float over the page. Real elevation, kept tight. - **Knob** (`0 1px 2px light-dark(rgba(16,24,40,0.18), rgba(0,0,0,0.4))`): the moving part of a control, such as a switch's knob. - **Lift** (`0 1px 2px light-dark(rgba(16,24,40,0.08), rgba(0,0,0,0.3))`): the barely-there separation on a raised strip. - **Overlay** (`light-dark(rgba(0,0,0,0.45), rgba(0,0,0,0.6))`): the modal scrim. Deeper in dark on purpose: black reads lighter against a dark backdrop and needs more alpha to still dim.
